CHAPTER 01材料背景
01
塑料依赖与现有处理路径

材料背景

先理解材料的规模，以及难以消失的废弃物。

项目从塑料的生产与废弃问题切入，对照便利性与处理难度。生产量、回收量和去向被放在一起，形成最初的问题背景。

5 亿吨全球年塑料生产量 / 项目资料

微塑料不只留在垃圾场，也进入日常环境。

空气、水体、土壤和人体相关研究，使塑料污染从可见的垃圾进一步延伸到难以察觉的颗粒。这里的影像是议题研究的视觉参照。

设计记录 / Original notes ＋

Microplastics have been found in the atmosphere, oceans, soil, and even in human blood and placentas.

处理方式各不相同，却没有让塑料轻易消失。

项目研究比较随意丢弃、焚烧、回收和填埋四种去向。这些比例是创作阶段收集的二手资料，用来说明现有处理路径的局限。

减量、限制、宣传与替代，各自解决了什么？

我将已有应对方式按措施、参与情况和效果进行对照：个人减量带来回收上的进展，限塑减少袋类废弃物，公益宣传提升环境意识，研究机构则持续探索生物塑料。

CHAPTER 02多方访谈
02
从现实冲突提出问题

多方访谈

同一种材料，在不同使用者眼中有不同价值。

访谈记录呈现三种立场：配送依赖包装的成本与密封性；医疗使用重视无菌、安全和便利；环境研究关注生产、使用和废弃的全链条影响。它们共同揭示了材料依赖背后的现实冲突。

配送视角

Master Li

包装需要经济、密封且不易破损。漏液和损坏也会转化为配送员的赔付与评价压力。
医疗使用视角

Dr. Liu

一次性耗材的无菌、防漏和便利性，关系到患者安全与感染控制。
环境研究视角

Professor Zheng

影响贯穿生产、使用与废弃，并通过微塑料累积延伸至生态与人体环境。
设计记录 / Original notes ＋

Name: Master Li，Occupation: Food delivery rider

Plastic is considered the most economical and practical option for ensuring delivery efficiency and safety. Paper or early biodegradable meal boxes are prone to damage and leakage; if problems arise, delivery personnel may be liable for compensation and face the risk of negative reviews.

Medical plastics are regarded as a core medium for ensuring diagnostic and treatment safety and controlling infections, possessing irreplaceable value. Items such as disposable syringes, infusion sets, and medical consumables have characteristics such as sterility, leak resistance, and ease of use, which are directly related to patient safety and the occupational protection of healthcare workers.

It is believed that plastic pollution poses a full-chain threat far beyond traditional perceptions. At the production stage, the extraction and synthesis of plastic raw materials emit toxic and harmful gases; at the usage stage, excessive consumption of disposable plastics exacerbates resource wastage; at the disposal stage, plastic waste is difficult to degrade, accumulating and breeding bacteria, polluting groundwater, and flowing into the oceans to form microplastics, which, through bioaccumulation in the food chain, threaten both ecosystems and human living environments.

Name: Dr. Liu，Profession: Emergency Department Physician

Name: Professor Zheng，Occupation: Professor in Environmental Science

从“消除塑料”，转向对“共存叙事”的质疑。

研究将我带向一个更不安的问题：如果摆脱塑料的努力不足，人类是否可能反过来将它描述成一种好东西？“与塑料共存”成为未来推演的起点。

设计记录 / Original notes ＋

Since humans cannot get rid of plastic, we will consider how to coexist with it

Conclusion

Humanity is unable to effectively manage plastic recycling, and plastic pollution has become an urgent issue

CHAPTER 03未来推演
03
技术、权力与欲望的故事

未来推演

让一个荒诞的承诺，沿着权力与欲望传播。

以下是一组虚构的未来推演：污染持续存在，微塑料进入人体；政府与学术背书为材料赋予新的意义；资本推出培养装置，公众则追逐它承诺的“永恒”。这些人物与场景是叙事拼贴，并不代表真实的政策或技术背书。

设计记录 / Original notes ＋

Insufficient human action and inadequate measures in the future will result in plastic waste not being effectively managed

A large amount of plastic pollutes the human living environment, and microplastics accumulate in the human body

Human governments, in order to shirk responsibility, promote the idea that microplastics can form a protective shell for cells

At the same time, the government is seeking scholars to endorse microplastics

Once the plastic cell culture device was launched, it was highly sought after, and the product became a new trend

Launch a plastic cell culture device, promoting the idea that it can transform the plastic in the body into a highly protective cellular shell, allowing cells to persist like plastic and potentially achieve immortality

八格故事，完整展开“塑料细胞”的未来。

故事从污染环境开始，经过人类尝试“消化”塑料、提出塑料细胞、培养与细胞保护壳的设定，最终走向“永生”与产品热潮。它不是生物医学方案，而是把技术语言如何制造欲望的过程变成可以观看的寓言。

设计记录 / Original notes ＋

In the future, plastic waste has already polluted the human living environment.

The Birth of the Concept of Plastic Cells: Humanity's Attempt to Integrate Plastic with Cells

The plastic cell is coated with a layer of plastic on the outside of its biological cell membrane.

At the same time, those who underwent the plastic cell experiment gained 'immortality'.

Humankind has begun attempting to 'digest' plastic, integrating it into daily life and the human body.

Humans successfully cultured plastic cells using a plastic cell incubator.

Plastic cells combine the characteristics of plastics that are not easily decomposed, making them resistant to aging under natural conditions and impervious to bacterial attack.

Therefore, plastic cell culture vessels have been widely sought after.

CHAPTER 04概念与形态
04
从视觉语言到设备外形

概念与形态

以实验室和消费承诺，构成机器的可信外观。

我把塑料、工业设备、实验室、胶囊与幸福生活的图像并置，寻找一套既像科学设备、又像可消费商品的视觉语言。培养装置借助容器、液体、屏幕和运动部件，让观众进入这套未来设定。

设计记录 / Original notes ＋

As plastic is difficult to be decomposed, micro plastic is found in human body. I wonder what if it is not a bad news but a good news.

The Capital may see it as an opportunity to invent a new machine that used micro plastic to produce medicine that could mix with our cells as shell. In this way, cells could be protected from virus, germs, and even self destruction.

In this way, eternity may arrive.

完整设计记录

按项目版面阅读背景、概念、制作与成果的原文记录。

封面1＋

Plastic Eternity

Plastic pollution is one of the most serious pollution in the world. Though people are aware of the negative impact, few effective solutions are executed as recycling and processing the waste means high cost and little benefit from the business perspective.

Based on the situation, I proposed a novel machine that could use micro plastic to build the shell for cells inside our body. On the one hand, the plastic could provide adequate protection for cells from being damaged and could live longer to keep human young. On the other hand, the eternity could bring great business value for companies.

Through the project, I want to ask if this is only a hilarious idea that may exist in our head, or it may seriously become a future.

AFTERWORD / 创作之后CHEN HAO

Artist Statement.

在制作、倾听与重新思考之间。

我的创作始于一个问题：我们为改善日常生活而建立的系统，如何影响人的行为、选择与关系？在福建理工大学学习产品设计的过程中，我逐渐开始关注这些系统内部的矛盾：塑料带来便利，却不断积累为废弃物；公共空间对不同人群的接纳程度并不相同；教育标准也可能忽略个体的真实感受。我希望通过设计，让这些矛盾变得可以被感知、质疑和讨论。

我的实践涉及思辨产品、公共服务、游戏和可穿戴装置。我通常从背景研究、观察与访谈开始，再将发现转化为情境、规则、形态和交互。制作也是我思考的重要方式。搭建模型、连接传感器或测试游戏，常常能揭示仅凭图纸无法发现的问题。作品集中的四个项目均由我独立完成，让我能够从最初的研究出发，持续推进设计、原型制作与最终展示。

在《Plastic Eternity》中，我构想了一台将微塑料转化为人体细胞保护壳的虚构机器，借助“永生”的承诺，探讨环境危机如何可能被重新包装为商业机会。《Urban Respite Initiative》则回应香港城市生活中更直接的休憩需求。通过连接座椅、占用信息、预约和导航，我探索一套服务如何同时支持游客的短暂停留，以及外籍家庭佣工周期性的社交聚会。

在《Azure Clean》中，参与被转化为一场关于海岸污染的桌游。卡牌与行动后果让玩家思考个人行为与共同环境之间的联系。《The Armor of Form》则通过一件限制手部动作、同时不断给予赞美的可穿戴装置，制造身体感受与外部认可之间的不协调，追问当“正确姿势”成为衡量创作表现的标准时，我们可能失去什么。

这些项目让我逐渐认识到，创作者希望表达的内容，并不一定会被参与者以同样的方式理解。游戏可能变得难以掌握，思辨装置可能显得过于可信，服务也可能引入新的门槛。因此，反馈和修改是我创作过程中不可缺少的部分。

我希望自己的作品经过细致推敲，也为不同的理解保留空间。通过研究生阶段的学习，我希望加强研究方法，深化对互动媒体的理解，并探索实体与数字体验如何同时支持批判性思考和有意义的参与。对我而言，未来的创作将持续发生在制作、倾听与重新思考之间，不断探索设计能够带来的可能。

My practice begins with a question: how do the systems we create to improve everyday life shape our behaviour, choices, and relationships? Studying Product Design at Fujian University of Technology, I have become interested in the tensions within these systems: plastics that offer convenience but accumulate as waste, public spaces that accommodate some people more easily than others, and educational standards that can overlook individual experience. I use design to make these tensions tangible, giving people something they can encounter, question, and discuss.

My work moves between speculative products, public services, games, and wearable installations. I begin with contextual research, observation, and interviews, then translate what I find into scenarios, rules, forms, and interactions. Making is an important part of my thinking. Building a model, connecting a sensor, or testing a game often reveals questions that drawings alone cannot answer. All four projects in this portfolio were developed independently, allowing me to follow each inquiry from initial research through design, prototyping, and presentation.

In Plastic Eternity, I imagine a fictional machine that transforms microplastics into protective shells for human cells. The promise of immortality becomes a way to examine how an environmental crisis might be repackaged as a commercial opportunity. Urban Respite Initiative addresses a more immediate situation: the need for accessible places to rest in Hong Kong. By connecting seating, occupancy information, booking, and navigation, I explore how a service might accommodate both tourists’ short visits and domestic workers’ recurring social gatherings.

Participation takes a different form in Azure Clean, a board game about coastal pollution. Its cards and consequences invite players to consider the relationship between individual actions and a shared environment. In The Armor of Form, a wearable device constrains hand movements while delivering praise, creating an uneasy relationship between bodily comfort and external approval. It asks what may be lost when “correct” posture becomes a measure of creative achievement.

Across these projects, I am learning that an intended message does not guarantee a shared understanding. A game can become difficult to follow; a speculative object can appear too persuasive; a service can introduce new barriers. These possibilities make feedback and revision essential to my practice.

I want to develop work that is thoughtful in its construction and open to different interpretations. Through postgraduate study, I hope to strengthen my research methods, deepen my understanding of interactive media, and explore how physical and digital experiences can support both critical reflection and meaningful participation. I see my future practice as an ongoing exchange between making, listening, and reconsidering what design makes possible.
